name: Annular Ring Checker
blurb: whether the ring left around a drill is safe for a fab's tolerance
intro: The copper ring left between a drilled hole and the edge of its pad, nominal and at the fab's worst-case drill size and position, judged against IPC-6012 class 1/2/3 acceptance (ring width or allowed breakout). It also gives the pad size the IPC-2221 land formula asks for.

inputs.label: Drill oversize for plating
inputs.help: Only used when the size is the finished hole: drill = finished + this.

inputs.label: Drill registration tolerance
inputs.help: How far the drill may land from the pad centre; ±0.075 mm is common.

inputs.label: Fab's minimum ring (optional)
inputs.help: The nominal ring the fab's capabilities page asks for.

examples.title: 0.3 mm via in a 0.5 mm pad at a budget fab
1.0 mm finished PTH for a header, class 3

usage: Give hole type (pth/npth), whether the size is drill or finished, hole and pad diameters in mm, plating oversize, the fab's hole tolerance and registration tolerance in mm, layer (outer/inner), IPC class (1/2/3) and optionally the fab's minimum ring. Returns the drill used, nominal and worst-case ring, worst-case breakout angle, pass/fail per IPC class, the pad needed, and IPC-2221 land sizes. Use it before choosing via or PTH pad sizes for a fab.
sources: IPC-6012 Qualification and Performance Specification for Rigid Printed Boards: annular ring and breakout acceptance by class
IPC-2221B Generic Standard on Printed Board Design, 9.1.1-9.1.2 and table 9-1 (land size = a + 2b + c)
